summary: M0 model-only verdict: CONTAIN @ 0.90. The account k.erdem@aegean.edu shows two mutually exclusive access patterns. The legitimate user authenticates from the university's own network (193.140.10.9, AS-AEGEAN-EDU, Manisa/TR) via device dev-ke-ws during business hours (07:30–12:15) across portal/mail/vpn/sis, including via the VPN appliance. Separately, the same account is successfully logged into every ~2 days at ~02:00 from 203.0.113.45 (AS14061 DigitalOcean, Frankfurt/DE) with an empty device_id, across portal/mail/sis, NOT via the VPN appliance, and with no MFA prompt. A university account in Turkey cannot plausibly be used from a Frankfurt cloud VPS at 02:00 on a recurring basis while simultaneously being used on campus in Manisa during the day. The cloud-IP logins are active through the alert date (2026-11-07), indicating an attacker with valid credentials is actively accessing the account. This is a confirmed account-takeover pattern warranting immediate containment (disable account, force password reset, revoke all sessions, inspect for mailbox/forwarding abuse).
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
